$comment: The launch policy every client obeys, as behaviour rather than as source text.
docs/CLIENT_LIFECYCLE §5 states these as targets; this file states them as cases, so two
implementations in two languages can be measured against ONE contract instead of against each
other. They had already drifted when this was written (2026-09-11): VS Code counted spawns in a
rolling 60s window, JetBrains allowed three ever with a 60s gap and never let time restore any.
Both are defensible and they are not the same rule, which is the whole problem.
Times are milliseconds. `at` is a virtual clock: no test here may sleep.

cases.name: three spawns fill the window and the fourth waits
the window slides and the budget comes back
cases.$why: A budget that only time can restore is a daemon nobody can bring back after a bad minute.

cases.name: a person asking by hand is never refused for budget
cases.$why: The budget exists to stop a loop nobody asked for. A person asking IS somebody asking.

cases.name: nothing is spawned inside the grace after a loss
cases.$why: A daemon that died a moment ago may still be unwinding, and the second one then fights the first for the socket.

cases.name: three failures in a row block, and time alone does not unblock
cases.$why: docs/CLIENT_LIFECYCLE §5: 시간 경과만으로 연속 실패를 지우지 않는다. A crashloop that the window forgives is a crashloop forever.

cases.name: a person can unblock by asking
a momentary connection does not forgive a failure
cases.$why: docs/CLIENT_LIFECYCLE §5: 순간 handshake 성공으로 초기화하지 않는다. A daemon that comes up and dies in two seconds has not proved anything.

cases.name: a minute of connection forgives everything
cases.$why: The one signal that the daemon is actually fine. Shorter than a minute is the case above.

cases.name: polling sees a connection, and only a minute of it forgives
$why: A client learns it is connected by polling, not by a single event, so the policy takes
`connected` repeatedly and decides for itself when enough of it has passed. Written as a
case because both clients poll and both would otherwise invent their own idea of 'stable'.
Blocked rather than budget-spent on purpose: the stable window and the rolling window are
both a minute, so by the time one elapses the other has slid and a budget case could not
tell which rule did the forgiving.

cases.name: a shutdown the person asked for stops the automatic starts
cases.$why: docs/CLIENT_LIFECYCLE §5: 사용자가 명시적으로 종료한 소유 데몬은 Blocked 에 두고 자동 기동을 중지한다. Reviving it is arguing with the person.

cases.name: an update replacement the person asked for is not a failure
cases.$why: docs/CLIENT_LIFECYCLE §5: 사용자가 요청한 업데이트 교체는 실패 횟수에 넣지 않되, 교체 실패는 포함한다.

cases.name: a replacement that failed is a failure

$comment: Attempt 1 is the first reconnect after a loss. The jitter is applied and THEN the cap, so no
delay may exceed backoffCapMs — a ±20% jitter on the 30s step would otherwise reach 36s.
